claim: The Pizol 5-lake hike covers 11.4 km with ~553 m ascent / ~911 m descent, takes 4.5 hours, is rated medium difficulty, and requires hikers to reach Gaffia chairlift by 16:30 or Pizolhütte by 16:00 to catch the last descent (Furt gondola 17:30).
quote: 11.4 km | Duration: 4.30 h | Elevation gain: 553m 911m ... Hikers must reach the Gaffia chairlift by 4:30 PM or Pizolhütte by 4:00 PM. The final gondola descent from Furt departs at 5:30 PM.

claim: Pizol's hiking and sightseeing season starts Ascension Day 14 May 2026 with daily Bad Ragaz gondola operation; all five summer lifts open daily from Saturday 27 June through Saturday 18 October 2026.
quote: The hiking and sightseeing season will kick off on Ascension Day, May 14, 2026, with the start of daily operations on the Bad Ragaz gondola. Starting Saturday, June 27, all five summer lifts at Pizol will open and operate daily through Saturday, October 18, 2026.

claim: The full 5-lake route is realistically accessible only from mid-July to mid-October because of lingering snow on the high traverse; even in July snowfields and névés often remain on the path.
quote: The hike will be accessible from mid-July to mid-October ... even in July during a heat wave, there was still snow on the path and several névés (snow patches) to cross.

claim: The Heidiweg is a 6.5 km easy circular walk from Maienfeld station through vineyards to Heididorf, Heidihof viewpoint and Heidi's fountain, taking about 1 h 30 min and marked with red 'Heidiweg' signs.
quote: Maienfeld station to Heididorf: approximately 40 minutes; Complete Heidiweg loop: approximately 1 hour 30 minutes; Total distance: 6.5 km ... signalized with red directional signs marked 'Heidiweg'

claim: A longer Heidi Adventure Trail continues from Heididorf up to Heidi-Alp on the Ochsenberg, climbing roughly 450 m with twelve themed stations and taking about 1 h 45 min one-way.
quote: the Heidi Adventure Trail to Heidialp takes around an hour and three quarters ... if you don't feel like hiking the 450 metres up to the Heidialp, you can follow the trail over fields and meadows to Hotel Restaurant Heidihof.

claim: Flumserberg cable cars (SeeJet sections 1-2, BergJet, Chrüz, Prodalp-Express, Prodkamm) close briefly 26-29 May 2026 for the seasonal switch, then resume partial operation the following weekend ahead of full summer service.
quote: All facilities, including GB SeeJet, will be closed from Tuesday, May 26 to Friday, May 29, 2026. Partial operations will resume next weekend.

claim: Flumserberg opens partial summer operations over Whitsun weekend 23-25 May 2026 with tobogganing, climbing, biking and hiking up to ~1500 m, then commences daily operation including BergJet on 6 June 2026.
quote: The summer season will begin with partial operations over the Whitsun weekend (23–25 May 2026) ... Daily operation, including the BergJet gondola, will commence on June 6, 2026.

claim: The Walensee north-shore hike from Weesen via Betlis and the Seerenbachfälle waterfalls to car-free Quinten is a moderate ~3.5-4 hour route with ~500 m elevation gain along forested cliff paths.
quote: The Weesen - Quinten via Lake Walen is considered a moderate route with an elevation gain of 1,633 ft, taking approximately 3.5–4 hr to complete.

claim: Quinten is reachable only on foot or by Walensee ferry and is known for its Mediterranean microclimate with terraced vineyards and fig trees, making the shore hike viable already in late spring.
quote: Quinten Village is accessible only by foot or boat, this secluded lakeside hamlet is renowned for its Mediterranean microclimate, terraced vineyards, and fig trees

claim: The Falknis (2,562 m) on the Swiss-Liechtenstein border above Maienfeld is a demanding T4-level alpine hike requiring sure-footedness, taking 5-7 hours and rewarding climbers with views as far as Lake Constance.
quote: Falknis is on the border between Liechtenstein and Switzerland ... lies at 2,560 m above sea level. The view from Falknis extends northward beyond Lake Constance ... For the downhill variant you can calculate 5 to 6 hours, if you want to hike uphill the other way around, you should calculate 7 hours.

claim: The Alvier summit (2,343 m) above Sevelen offers a 360° panorama across Walensee, the Rhine valley and Lake Constance via an exposed rocky trail from Windegg through Alp Arin requiring sure-footedness.
quote: summit at 2,342 meters offers a 360-degree panorama over Lake Walen, the Rhine Valley, and all the way to Lake Constance ... starts in Windegg and then over the Alp Arin at 1518m and then up to the Alvier mountain peak at 2343m.
